scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Use the last two bits as the state: eight clusters shrink to four states, halving Viterbi work

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: each circle is a state with two outgoing arrows; label $I=d/\omega_j$ gives the new bit $d$ and the cluster used by that branch; the table is the same transition table.

scene-u01-pnew1-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew1-45.text: Self-loops at top left and bottom right use $\omega_1$ and $\omega_8$

scene-u01-pnew1-84.name: text#84
scene-u01-pnew1-84.text: "The state is a value measured from the channel" is wrong: it is the bit pattern in channel memory, which cannot be measured; only noisy samples $x_k$ can.

scene-u01-pnew1-86.name: text#86
scene-u01-pnew1-86.text: Table matches the lecture, listed by code

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Scalar hand calculation: point-wise gives $1,1,1,1$, Viterbi backtracks $1,0,1,1$, correcting $I_2$

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: each column top is the sample value, node numbers are minimum cumulative costs (smaller is better); the thick green line is the backtracked path; the three rows below compare decisions.

scene-u01-pnew2-103.name: text#103
scene-u01-pnew2-103.text: Smaller cost is better (squared distance), opposite to the KP04 score; red: wrong bits

scene-u01-pnew2-112.name: text#112
scene-u01-pnew2-112.text: $0.70$ is closer to center $0.5$ ($0.2$) than to $1.0$ ($0.3$), so $I_2$ is wrong.

scene-u01-pnew2-116.name: text#116
scene-u01-pnew2-116.text: Minimum cost $0.0975$; backtracking gives $1,0,1,1$, the true bits.

scene-u01-pnew2-117.name: text#117
scene-u01-pnew2-117.text: Brute force over $16$ bit strings also gives $0.0975$

scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: At noise $\sigma=0.2$, the error rate drops from $12.5\%$ to $0.375\%$, about $33\times$ fewer

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: each pair has two bars, thick red for point-wise nearest center, green for state-trellis Viterbi; shorter means fewer errors; the right gives limits and failure cases.

scene-u01-pnew3-8.name: text#8
scene-u01-pnew3-8.text: Two decoders on the same data ($20{,}001$ bits)

scene-u01-pnew3-31.name: text#31
scene-u01-pnew3-31.text: Bar length: error rate (wrong bits divided by $20{,}001$)

scene-u01-pnew3-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew3-49.text: There are $2^{n+l-2}$ states: each increase in channel memory $n$ or samples $l$ doubles them, and Viterbi cost grows too.

scene-u01-pnew3-53.name: text#53
scene-u01-pnew3-53.text: The view that hidden states drive observations is the core of next week's hidden Markov models.
